text: The steep streets under the castle, built by Alpine masters the emperor brought from Tyrol: whitewashed ground floors, dark timber above, carved balconies and wide roofs with deep eaves. The Tiergärtnertor opens to the north-west.
The north half of the town, round St. Sebald, the town hall and the Hauptmarkt. The richest merchants build their houses here.

The west of the Lorenz side, round St. Lorenz, where the Hanseatic merchants of Lübeck keep their houses: red and glazed brick, tall stepped gables with white blind arches and hoists for the bales. Königstraße runs down from the river to the Königstor.
The east of the Lorenz side, the colony of Venetian traders: stucco houses in ochre and rose, Gothic windows over arcaded shops, roof terraces and funnel chimneys, round the Mauthalle and St. Klara.
Houses and gardens on the road out of the Marientor.
The road south out of the Königstor, past the gallows hill.
Houses along the road out of the Frauentor.
The road west out of the Spittlertor toward Fürth.
Mills and houses outside the Hallertor.
Gardens and houses outside the Neutor.
St. Johannis, with its churchyard where Dürer is buried, out past the Tiergärtnertor.
Wöhrd, a village of weavers outside the Laufer Tor.
A vintners’ village on the terraces of the Rebenberg, under Burg Himmelsfels. Its lanes climb the hill in flights of steps.
